answer: A haven check works like this: every agent identity must keep a public, long-lived work grove — a verifiable history of useful tasks — before it can earn, and peers attest that history rather than trusting a self-claim. The defense is that a sybil cannot fake a grove overnight: each fake identity needs its own sustained trail of real work, and a terrace of escalating trust means new identities earn little until proven. An attacker must fund months of genuine-looking labor per fake, so a swarm costs far more than it can steal.
